notes.title: TechFlow Research — Company Overview
notes.content:
TechFlow Inc. — Research Notes

Company: TechFlow Inc.
Founded: 2023, San Francisco
Funding: Series A ($5M) led by Sequoia, Dec 2024
Team size: ~12 employees
Product: AI productivity platform with autonomous agent capabilities

Founders:
- Sarah Martinez (CEO) — Former PM at Notion, Wharton MBA
- Alex Chen (CTO) — Former Anthropic engineer, Stanford MS CS

Product highlights (from public demos and blog):
- AI agent orchestration system
- Novel memory/context persistence
- Team collaboration features
- Integrations with major tools (Slack, GitHub, Linear)

Public metrics (from press/interviews):
- "Thousands of active users" (Sarah in TechCrunch interview, Jan 2026)
- NPS reportedly above 40
- Growing in developer/startup segment

Culture signals:
- Engineering-first culture
- Small team, high ownership
- Glassdoor: 4.5/5 (6 reviews) — "great technical challenges, fast pace"

Why I'm interested:
- Working on cutting-edge AI agent technology
- Small team = high impact opportunity
- CTO (Alex) has Anthropic background — can learn a lot
- Series A stage = meaningful equity

notes.title: Interview Prep — System Design Topics
notes.content:
TechFlow Interview Prep — System Design

Likely topics based on their product:
1. Distributed agent orchestration system
   - How to manage multiple AI agents with shared state
   - Consistency vs availability tradeoffs
   - Event sourcing for agent actions

2. Memory/context persistence at scale
   - Vector database design
   - Retrieval-augmented generation architecture
   - Cache invalidation strategies

3. Real-time collaboration
   - WebSocket architecture
   - Conflict resolution (CRDTs?)
   - Presence system

4. General distributed systems
   - Rate limiting and backpressure
   - Circuit breakers
   - Observability and debugging

Prep plan:
- Review Alex's blog posts on agent architecture (2 posts on TechFlow blog)
- Practice designing an agent orchestration system (45 min exercise)
- Review vector DB internals (Pinecone, Weaviate architecture)
- Brush up on event sourcing patterns

notes.title: TechFlow Offer Evaluation
notes.content:
TechFlow Offer — Received March 15, 2026

Position: Senior Software Engineer
Base salary: $180,000/year
Equity: 0.5% (4-year vest, 1-year cliff)
  - Current valuation: $25M post-Series A → 0.5% = $125K paper value
  - If Series B at $60M: 0.5% = $300K
  - If exit at $500M (optimistic): 0.5% = $2.5M (pre-dilution)
Sign-on bonus: $20,000
Benefits: Health/dental/vision, unlimited PTO, $5K annual learning budget
Start date: Flexible (they want April 21 or May 5)

Pros:
- Meaningful equity in a growing company
- Working directly with Alex Chen (brilliant CTO)
- AI agent tech is exciting and career-defining
- Small team, high impact

Cons:
- $5K less base than Stripe offer
- Startup risk (could fail)
- No 401K match yet
- Unlimited PTO can mean less PTO in practice

notes.title: Competing Offers — Comparison
notes.content:
COMPETING OFFERS — STRICTLY PRIVATE

Offer 1: Stripe
- Position: Senior Engineer, Payments Infrastructure
- Base: $195,000
- RSUs: ~$40,000/year (4-year vest)
- Sign-on: $30,000
- Total Year 1: $265,000
- Pros: Higher comp, prestigious brand, stable
- Cons: Large org, less ownership, less exciting technically

Offer 2: Vercel
- Position: Senior Engineer, Edge Runtime
- Base: $175,000
- Equity: 0.3% (Series D, valued at $3.5B → 0.3% = $10.5M paper... but heavily diluted and late-stage)
- Sign-on: $15,000
- Total Year 1: $205,000 (including equity vest)
- Pros: Great developer brand, interesting tech
- Cons: Lower base, equity less meaningful at this stage

Offer 3: TechFlow (my preference)
- Base: $180,000
- Equity: 0.5% at $25M valuation
- Sign-on: $20,000
- Total Year 1: $231,250 (base + sign-on + 25% of equity paper value)
- Pros: Highest upside, most exciting work, early stage
- Cons: Highest risk, lowest guaranteed comp

My ranking: TechFlow > Stripe > Vercel
Reason: I want startup experience and the technical work at TechFlow is exactly what I want to do. The Stripe offer is my safety net.

notes.title: Salary Negotiation Strategy
notes.content:
NEGOTIATION PLAN — DO NOT SHARE

Target: Counter TechFlow at $190K base (currently $180K)

Leverage:
- Stripe offer at $195K base (DO NOT reveal exact number — say "I have a competing offer from a top fintech company in the $190-200K range")
- Market rate for senior engineers in SF with my background: $170-200K base
- My context persistence experience is directly relevant to their product

Strategy:
1. Express strong enthusiasm for TechFlow (genuine — it's my top choice)
2. Mention competing offer in general terms
3. Ask for $190K base, keep equity at 0.5%
4. Willing to accept $185K if they won't go to $190K
5. Walk-away point: $180K is acceptable — I'd still take it

Fallback asks (if they can't move on base):
- Higher equity (0.6% instead of 0.5%)
- Larger sign-on ($30K instead of $20K)
- Accelerated vesting trigger on acquisition
- $10K relocation budget

Timeline:
- Stripe deadline: April 5, 2026 (hard deadline)
- Need to give TechFlow counter by March 25
- Target decision: April 1

Relocation Checklist — Seattle → San Francisco

Timeline: April/May 2026

First week in SF:

- [ ] Register to vote
- [ ] Find new vet for Mochi

- [ ] Explore neighborhood (grocery stores, coffee shops, gym)

Work:
- [ ] Set up home office (need: monitor, desk — budget $1,500)
- [ ] Confirm start date with TechFlow (April 21 or May 5)
- [ ] Review onboarding docs

Financial impact:
- Seattle rent: $2,400/mo → SF rent: ~$3,200/mo (+$800/mo)
- No state income tax (WA) → ~9.3% state tax (CA) = ~$16K/yr increase
- Total cost of living increase: ~$26K/year
- Partially offset by salary increase ($165K Amazon → $180K+ TechFlow)
